items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: J. J. Johnson joined me in Indianapolis [Indiana] and came to California with me.

ctx.x: You just mentioned that a lot of people were getting drafted. Was that the only reason these people came in, or did you want to inject a different kind of sound or you were attracted to some of these younger musicians?

No, but, I mean, some of those I replaced because they went into the service. But, no, I don’t know. Just, you know, J. J. Johnson joined me in Indianapolis [Indiana] and came to California with me. Now, when Max Roach came into the band, I don’t remember. Miles Davis was in the band in ’46, something, and he was with it for just a short time, maybe a matter of weeks.
You picked him up in St. Louis [Missouri], is that correct?

items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I went to this rehearsal a nervous wreck, to try out for this job and how I got through and managed I don’t know, but Benny hired me.

ctx.x: [laughs]. How did your opportunity to go with Benny Carter come about?

It seems that Benny came through Indianapolis, to perform in Indianapolis or something like that – I’m not clear on that – and needed a trombonist. Someone, I never knew who – someone or some faction got his ear and said, There’s a kid here in town that you may want to consider." I got a call from Benny Carter’s manager to come to a rehearsal and try out for the job. I went to this rehearsal a nervous wreck, to try out for this job and how I got through and managed I don’t know, but Benny hired me.
I hear it Earl Coleman might have been the one that put the bug in Benny’s ear.

items.q: Actually, J.J. Johnson joined the band in 1942, in September

ctx.x: And Freddie Webster. Actually, J.J. Johnson joined the band in 1942, in September, when we were
on the way to California, we picked up J.J. Johnson in Indianapolis.
